apps.disagreement_reason: The human's note is about the app looking old (a CD-player-style skin, old UI framework). The rubric lists looking dated as not a defect. Nothing measurable supports a 0: there is no truncation, overlap, broken image or unreadable text, and the logo overlap in the top right is branding artwork. The inspector did miss one small measurable flaw. On the selected 'Sing' tile, white text sits on pale blue (126,197,234) at about 1.9:1. The pale-blue subtitle on the mid-blue background is about 2.4:1. Both are large text and still readable, so they are minor. That moves the score from 2 to 1, not to 0. The rest of the gap is taste.

defects.reason: The name heading really breaks mid-word ('Gottheim' / 'er') with no hyphen, because the card's name column is narrow. The name is still easy to read as 'Gottheimer', so this is a visible flaw that does not stop reading. It should be minor, not major.
Every Date cell wraps a short date onto three lines ('Aug' / '14,' / '2026'), while wide columns such as Asset have spare room. This is a column that is too narrow. Minor is right.
Every Filing cell wraps onto three lines plus the arrow on a fourth ('Sep' / '15,' / '2026' / arrow). Real and minor.

apps.disagreement_reason: This is not taste: all three listed wraps are real, measurable defects, and the human's 2 overlooks them. The inspector's error is severity. It called the mid-word name break major, which forced a 0. The name stays readable, so the break is minor, and with only minor defects the rule gives 1. The inspector also missed a minor flaw that does not change the score: the Filing links are dark blue on near-black. As captured they are about 1.5:1, because the table is at half opacity while it shows 'Updating…'. Even at full opacity they would be only about 2.4:1. The correct score is 1. The inspector's 0 comes from severity inflation, and the human's 2 ignores real minor wraps.
The empty-state card is clean. The single word 'one.' wrapping to a second line is a normal line wrap, not a bad_wrap.

Nothing measurable. The very tight tracking on the headline is a display-type style choice. The small grey subreddit labels belong to a decorative animation and are about 4.2:1. The chat bubble does not cover any content.

apps.disagreement_reason: The controls are clean. The bottom of the preview being cut off in image 1 is just the page fold. In the rendered ring text, though, the letters look like they are placed at equal angles whatever their width. The wide 'C' and 'K' collide, while large gaps open around each narrow 'I', so the text reads as 'PICKF IT593278'. These uneven gaps between letters are measurable, and this is the tool's core output. It is still readable, so minor.

defects.reason: The central diagram view really is cut off on its right side. The canvas has no vertical scrollbar, the horizontal scrollbar has no right arrow, the folio navigation buttons after the '1 -' tab are missing, and the project tab text stops at '/ho'. The dock is not floating over the canvas, though. The docks take up most of the 852px-wide window and the central widget is squeezed below its minimum width, so the right kind is 'clipped' rather than 'overlap'. The box marks the Collections dock, not the cut edge. Major is defensible because the work area's scrolling and folio controls are hidden. The window is the app's own default size; the sandbox's lack of a window manager only stops anyone from enlarging it.

Several tree items are elided with '...' ('"ISO7200_A4_V1" tem...', '"page_de garde" temp...', '"Societe-pour-Alstom2...', '"Societe-pour-SNCF2" ...'). Real and minor. The box is misplaced, though: it sits on the '"DIN_A4" template' row, which is not truncated.
The project tab title is cut off mid-path ('Project « diagram : /ho') with no ellipsis, next to the tab scroll arrows. Real and minor. It has the same root cause as defect 1.

apps.disagreement_reason: The score is right, but defect 1 is mislabeled (it is clipping, not a floating overlap) and defect 2's box is on the wrong row.

defects.reason: The 'Your Heavy Duty Mixes' heading just sits at the scroll fold, under the fixed 'Nothing Playing' bar. Content always scrolls beneath a fixed player bar, and scrolling clears it. The heading is still readable. This comes from where the viewport happens to end, not from a layout fault. Even if counted, it would be minor, not major.
The card title is truncated with an ellipsis ('Somebody's Watchi...') by the card width. That fits the rubric's text_cut_off. Minor.
'Global Top 50 Trending' is a horizontally scrolling row of 50 items. A next card peeking at the right edge is the intended scroll cue, a layout choice that works, not a clipped control.
